- **self**: Partial unique indexes for soft delete (6/2)

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB's planner uses a partial index for a read only when the query predicate implies the partial filter or a stricter subset; this affects read-index eligibility, while the unique partial constraint still governs writes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/ · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/, https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2025-12-15-mongodb-partial-indexes/view, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/which-index-is-better-to-use-in-the-following-case/115928, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/
- [statement] A March 2019 Stack Overflow query-plan report found that { soft_deleted_at: null } still produced a FETCH filter because the [null, null] index bounds also included undefined or missing values. Treat this as a version-specific example and inspect explain() when active documents may have both null and missing states. (low confidence) (verified as of 2019-03-04) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54985673/mongodb-partial-indexes-avoid-filtering-stage-when-filtering-on-null-date · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] If a deleted record's key has been reused, restoring it to the active state makes it match the partial index again; MongoDB then rejects the restore with a duplicate-key error while another active record owns that key. The application needs a restore-conflict policy. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/ · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-soft-deletes/view, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/
- [statement] Before building a partial unique index, remove duplicate keys among documents that match its active-state filter. MongoDB cannot build a unique index when existing indexed documents violate the key constraint. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/ · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB enforces a unique constraint only among documents that match the partialFilterExpression. A soft-delete index such as { email: 1 } with unique: true and partialFilterExpression: { deletedAt: null } allows an active record to reuse an email after the old record receives a deletion timestamp, provided null represents the active state. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/ · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-soft-deletes/view, https://grasp-it.dev/mongodb/lesson/137/mongodb-indexes-and-query-plans-compound-multikey-unique-ttl-text-geospatial-partial-and-explain/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/
- [statement] For tenant-scoped uniqueness, use the tenant and normalized identifier as the compound unique key, such as { tenantId: 1, emailNormalized: 1 }, and use the soft-delete state in the partial filter. MongoDB applies compound uniqueness to the combination of indexed key values. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/ · keywords: Partial unique indexes for soft delete · also: https://grasp-it.dev/mongodb/lesson/137/mongodb-indexes-and-query-plans-compound-multikey-unique-ttl-text-geospatial-partial-and-explain/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/
